language.name: English
language.title: Language of the page
app.title: XsdViewer
menu.openFolder.title: Open every schema (*.xsd) of a folder and its sub-folders as a workspace named after the folder
menu.open.title: Choose schema files (through the server's own dialog when it has a display, so that their location is known and links can be followed)
menu.newWorkspace.title: Start an empty workspace: a new group of tabs
menu.openWorkspace.title: Open a saved workspace (*.xsdviewer.json) as a new group of tabs — several workspaces can be open together
menu.saveWorkspace.title: Save the location of the files of the active workspace in a workspace file (its own file is proposed)
menu.closeWorkspace.title: Close the active workspace and all its tabs
dialogs.unavailable: The server has no display: files are chosen in the browser, workspaces are unavailable
menu.quit.title: Stop the XsdViewer server and close this page
menu.autoStop: Stop the server when the last page is closed
menu.autoStop.title: On: the server exits by itself 15 seconds after the last page showing it has been closed (a reload or a restart of the browser reconnects in time). Off: it keeps running until File ▸ Quit or Ctrl+C, e.g. to reach it from another computer. Kept for the next runs; --keep-alive and --no-browser on the command line turn it off for a run.
menu.theme.title: Switches the page's colours between light and dark (the system's setting until you choose). Remembered by this browser.
settings.autoStop.on: The server will stop by itself once the last page has been closed
settings.autoStop.off: The server keeps running when the last page is closed: stop it with File ▸ Quit
about.title: XsdViewer
about.description: Web-based viewer for XML Schema files: the graph of the schema objects and their links, and the source text.
view.model.title: What a document of the selected declaration holds: its sequences, choices, elements and attributes as a tree, left to right, each named type opened on demand — the shape of the data
view.text.title: The source of the file, with its line numbers and its syntax coloured; the selected declaration is highlighted, and Ctrl+F searches the text
view.graph.title: How the declarations of the file refer to one another, around the selected one: what it leads to on the right, what uses it on the left, one step at a time — the map of the file
model.empty: No content model: a simple type, an attribute, or a declaration that names nothing else.
model.expandAll: Open every type, group and base type (six levels at most)
export.svg.title: Save the graph as an SVG file: a vector image, for documents
export.title: Export the current view as a PNG image
tab.new.title: New tab
empty.title: Open an XSD file
empty.hint: File ▸ Open… (Ctrl+O), or drop a file anywhere in this window.
drop.hint: Drop the XSD file to open it
graph.back.title: Back to the previous node
graph.twoLevels.title: Also show what the linked objects link to (a further column on the right)
legend.mandatory.title: A plain arrow is a mandatory link (minimum 1). The number after a link's name is its cardinality: 1, 0..1, 1..*…
legend.optional.title: A dashed arrow is an optional link: minOccurs 0, optional attribute, branch of a choice
graph.types.title: Which objects the graph draws: switch a type off to clear the view — the built-in types among them (kept for the next times)
graph.links.title: Which links the graph draws: switch a category off to clear the view (kept for the next times)
legend.choice.title: The element is one branch of an xs:choice (an xs:all is marked ○); an unmarked one follows an xs:sequence
legend.listUnion.title: A diamond instead of the arrowhead: the type is a list of the type it leads to (filled), or a union of the types it leads to (hollow)
legend.enum.title: The declaration enumerates its values: how many, at the bottom of its node (the values themselves in the tooltip and in the details panel)
legend.chain.title: The links of the file's own chain — a service to its operations and their messages, a phase to its patterns and their rules — drawn in colour: what leads to the schema objects stays grey
legend.derivation.title: A hollow arrowhead is a derivation: the type extends or restricts the type pointed to (its base type)
legend.model.chain.title: An object of the file's own chain, which is the model a WSDL or a Schematron has: a service holds its ports, a portType its operations, an operation its messages, a message the elements of its parts — where the schema's own content model takes over. The word above the name is the link's: the port's name, operation, input, fault, active, rule, assert…
legend.model.element.title: An element: its occurrences below the box, its type in the corner; dashed when optional. A named type, a global element (ref) is opened by its + handle
legend.model.base.title: The base type of the declaration: the type it extends or restricts, its content opened by the + handle
legend.model.group.title: A group the model refers to, its particles opened by the + handle
legend.model.attribute.title: An attribute: @name : type, ? when optional
legend.model.any.title: A wildcard (xs:any, xs:anyAttribute): the namespaces it accepts in the box
legend.model.compositor.title: A compositor, the particles it holds to its right: ··· xs:sequence (in order), ◇ xs:choice (one of them), ○ xs:all (each once, in any order); its occurrences below when not exactly one
legend.model.optional.title: A dashed box and link: minOccurs 0, or an optional attribute (?)
legend.model.occurs.title: Under a box, how many times it occurs: 0..1, 1..*, 2..5… Nothing when exactly one
legend.model.handle.title: The handle of a named type, a global element, a group or a base type: + opens its content, taken from its own declaration in this file or another of the workspace; − folds it. ⊞ opens them all
legend.model.recursive.title: The type is already open above in the tree: its content would repeat
files.title: Files
menu.openAll.title: Open in a tab every file of the workspace that is only listed in the Files panel (a large folder opens only its first file)
openAll.confirm: {0} files are listed: open them all as tabs?
menu.validate.title: Check an XML document against the shown schema — the XSD with the server's validator (its file on disk, imports included), the Schematron with its XPath 1.0 evaluator, both when the workspace holds the other one — in a tab of its own; needs the schema's location, so a file opened through File ▸ Open or a folder
validate.needsLocation: Validation needs the shown schema's location on disk (open it through File ▸ Open… or a folder) and an XML Schema or a Schematron, not a WSDL
validate.noneShown: No error; the other problems are hidden
validate.another.title: Choose another XML document to check against the same schemas
validate.rerun.title: Check the XML document again: read again from disk when it was chosen through the server's dialog (the schemas are always read again)
validate.errorsOnly.title: Hide the warnings, the informative reports and the expressions that could not be evaluated
validate.schema.title: The schema the document is checked against: any of the workspace's files of that kind with a location on disk
validate.path.title: The XML document's file, read again by ↻ Run again
validate.noPath: (opened in the browser: its folder is unknown)
validate.phase.title: The Schematron phase to run: a set of its patterns, or all of them
files.parsing.title: The objects of a file appear in the search once it is parsed; the list is redrawn as files come
files.failed.title: These files could not be parsed, so their objects answer no search: {0}
files.openAsWorkspace: Open the folder {0} as a workspace of its own
objects.title: Objects
info.title: Schema
details.xpath: The expression: a rule's context, an assertion's test
panel.resize: Drag to resize the panel (double-click: the default width, arrow keys when focused)
quit.confirm: Stop the XsdViewer server and close this page?
quit.stoppedHint: The server has been shut down; you can close this window.
external.noLocation: {0} is not declared in this file and no xs:import / xs:include says where it is: choose the file declaring it
folder.listed: {0} schemas of {1} listed in Files, {2} opened (open the others from there)
linked.listed.one: {0} linked schema found: listed in Files
linked.listed.other: {0} linked schemas found: listed in Files, open them from there
workspace.empty: No open file with a known location: nothing to save
workspace.listed: {0}: {1} files listed in Files, {2} opened (open the others from there)
workspace.close: Close the workspace {0} and its tabs
compare.button.title: Open the comparison: two declarations side by side, or two workspaces file by file
compare.clearSelection.title: No workspace selected for the file comparison any more
compare.title: Comparing {0} with {1}
comparison.close: Close the comparison and forget what it was comparing
comparison.chip.title: The comparison: a place of its own, not a workspace and not a file
comparison.files.title: Two workspaces file by file: what is identical, what differs, what only one of them has
comparison.objects.title: Two declarations side by side, wherever each of them lives: their content models, what differs marked
compare.selectTwo: Ctrl+click two workspace chips to compare their files: every file of either one, paired by name, and what differs in each pair.
compare.summary: {0} files: {1} identical, {2} different, {3} moved lines only, {4} only in {5}, {6} only in {7}
compare.sameModel: Same declarations and links: the texts differ elsewhere (documentation, layout, facets…)
compare.object.same: the same content model on both sides
compare.object.summary: {0} only on the left, {1} only on the right, {2} changed
compare.object.absent: This workspace does not declare it.
zoom.in: Draw it larger (the browser's own zoom is left alone)
zoom.reset: Back to the drawing's own size
objectCompare.title: {0} compared with {1}
objectCompare.noneMarked: Put a declaration on each side of this comparison, from the details panel of the one you are reading (◈ Left, ◈ Right). The two may be in different files, different workspaces, and bear different names; their content models are then drawn here side by side.
objectCompare.textSummary: {0} lines only on the left, {1} only on the right
objectCompare.textSame: The two are written the same way
objectCompare.graphSummary: {0} links only on the left, {1} only on the right
objectCompare.graphSame: The same links on both sides
objectCompare.oneMarked: One side is filled. Fill the other one from the details panel of a declaration (◈ Left or ◈ Right).
objectCompare.clear.title: Nothing marked for comparison any more
object.mark.title: Draw this declaration on the {0} of the comparison, in place of what that side holds
details.compare.hint: Draw this declaration beside another one, on the side you pick:
objectCompare.swap.title: Put each side where the other was
object.mark.off.title: The {0} of the comparison holds this declaration: click to take it off
compare.textTooLarge: Line by line comparison not shown: the files differ too much or are too large
compare.legend.title: Colours of the line by line comparison
compare.businessOnly.title: Ignore what does not define the schema: XML comments, xs:annotation (documentation, appinfo), the XML declaration, the xs:schema, xs:import and xs:include tags, blank lines and indentation
compare.diffOnly.title: Hide the identical files, and in a file's comparison show only the changed lines with one line of context
export.selectFirst: Select an object to export its graph
export.pngFailed: Could not create the PNG image
export.textTruncated: Text too long for one image: exported lines {0} to {1}
